answer: Reputation Ledge Pricing. Each identity's fee to send its first message equals a base rate divided by its accumulated non-transferable history depth, so new identities sit on a costly ledge while established ones pay near zero. Every additional identity an attacker creates resets that depth, making the marginal cost of the next sybil strictly higher than the last. One genuine sparrow account crosses the ridge once, but a thousand fakes each pay the full ledge premium forever.
